title: What a Shift and a Scale Do to the Four Summaries
unit: Mean, Median, Mode and Standard Deviation
quickIdea: The mean, median and mode follow y = ax + b exactly; the standard deviation follows |a| times the old one and takes no part of b.
remember: Mean, median and mode are equivariant: y-bar = a*x-bar + b, median(y) = a*median(x) + b, mode(y) = a*mode(x) + b.
Standard deviation: sd(y) = |a| * sd(x). Variance: Var(y) = a^2 * Var(x). There is no additive term in either.
The b disappears because a spread is measured from the centre, and the centre moved by exactly the same b.
For a > 0 the whole ordering is preserved, so the index position of the median and of the mode is unchanged. That is precisely the claim of GATE CSE 2011 Q.33.
For a < 0 the order reverses, so the index position flips: the value at position k moves to position n+1-k. The median value is still a*median + b, but it is no longer at the same index.
Writing sd(y) = a*sd(x) + b is the classic wrong option, and it is wrong for a reason worth remembering: a constant offset cannot widen or narrow a spread.
A scale factor a with |a| < 1 shrinks the spread; the absolute value is what handles a negative multiplier correctly.

example.prompt: X is 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Find the mean and standard deviation of Y = 3X - 5.
example.work: X has mean 6 and variance (16 + 4 + 0 + 4 + 16)/5 = 8, so sd(X) = 2.8284. Then mean(Y) = 3*6 - 5 = 13 and sd(Y) = 3*2.8284 = 8.4853. Directly, Y is 1, 7, 13, 19, 25 with mean 65/5 = 13, and the deviations -12, -6, 0, 6, 12 square to 144 + 36 + 0 + 36 + 144 = 360, giving a variance of 72 and a standard deviation of 8.4853. The two routes agree.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2011 Q.33 is this card. Four statements are offered about Y = a*x + b with a and b positive, and the incorrect one is sd(y) = a*sd(x) + b.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2011 Q.33: Y is formed from X by y_i = a*x_i + b with a, b positive. Which statement is INCORRECT - the index position of the mode is unchanged, the index position of the median is unchanged, mu_y = a*mu_x + b, or sigma_y = a*sigma_x + b?
variations.why: Each deviation x_i - mu_x becomes a*(x_i - mu_x), so the standard deviation is multiplied by a and nothing is added. With X = 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, a = 2 and b = 100, sd(X) = 1.0198 and sd(Y) = 2.0396, while 2*1.0198 + 100 would be 102.04.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Which of these are correct for a list of numbers? P: adding 7 to every entry adds 7 to the mean. Q: adding 7 to every entry adds 7 to the standard deviation. R: doubling every entry doubles the mean. S: doubling every entry leaves the standard deviation unchanged.
variations.why: The mean is equivariant under both a shift and a scale, so P and R hold. A shift leaves the standard deviation alone, so Q fails, and a scale multiplies it by the factor, so S fails.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A list has standard deviation 4. What is the standard deviation of -2X + 7?
variations.why: sd(-2X + 7) = |-2| * sd(X) = 2*4 = 8. The sign of the multiplier reverses the order of the values but cannot make a spread negative, which is why the absolute value appears.

trap.what: Writing sd(y) = a*sd(x) + b, or dropping the absolute value when a is negative.
trap.why: A spread is invariant under a shift, so b cannot enter the formula; and a spread is a distance, so a negative multiplier changes direction but not size.
trap.counterexample: X = 2, 3, 4, 4, 5 has sd 1.0198. With a = 2 and b = 100 the new sd is 2.0396, not 102.04. With a = -1 the new sd is still 1.0198, not -1.0198.

check.question: X has standard deviation 4. Find the standard deviation of Y = 0.5X + 100.
check.explanation: sd(Y) = |0.5| * sd(X) = 0.5*4 = 2. The 100 shifts every value and every mean equally, so it leaves the spread untouched.

visual.title: Mean, Median, Mode and Standard Deviation: Three Middles, One Spread, and When Each Rule Fails
covers: adding a constant moves the mean, median and mode and not sigma
scaling multiplies all three averages and sigma by the factor, sigma by |a|
a negative multiplier reverses the median index position
